p.t: Emerald Hill - The Little Nyonya Story
p.d: This 2025 edition of a Peranakan tale, spun off from the iconic The Little Nyonya, unfolds at Emerald Hill. An Ya, abducted from wealth, endures life in a brothel. Xin Niang, once a child beggar, blossoms into a refined lady. An Na, cast away as a jinx, returns to upend their lives. As secrets unravel, love and kinship are tested---will they rise above fate? 2025 年全新篇章，衍生自经典剧集《小娘惹》的传奇，重塑翡翠山娘惹大家族的兴衰荣辱。大户人家小姐安雅幼年被拐沦落妓院，际遇坎坷；流落街边的小乞丐心娘被大家族收养后蜕变为端庄淑女；从小被视为灾星的千金小姐安娜归来后心怀不轨。三人的命运在亲情，爱情中交织，纠缠不断。她们如何冲破枷锁，改变自己的人生？

The Middle East crisis and the resulting blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has caused supply disruptions for the globe, which can potentially lead to catastrophic consequences for modern civilization. The global economy, agriculture, energy production, and transportation infrastructure rely heavily on oil products such as petrol, diesel and liquified natural gas. So, is life without oil possible? A 4-part human interest series tries to answer this question as the filmmakers traverse Pakistan, Bangladesh, India, and Philippines to meet communities, governments and entrepreneurs building the future of human civilization with renewable energies like solar, biogas, organic fertilizers, and electric vehicles. We understand if this quiet transformation across Asia is sustainable and if life without oil can one day become a reality.

In this returning season of FINDING, six heartfelt reunions honour people who left a lasting mark. Nearly 40 years after Basic Military Training, Minister Ong Ye Kung searches for his BMT buddy Eric, while actor-host Noah Yap reunites with Ma’am Haiyan, the mentor who believed in him and supported his family through difficult times. Actor Elvin Ng and his mother travel to Indonesia to surprise Jumi, the domestic helper who became their pillar of strength, while 23-year-old Leticia journeys to Central Java to thank Auntie Mas, who helped raise her for 12 years. Dino Isaac reconnects with the Primary 3 teacher whose kindness gave him hope after a traumatic childhood, while radio DJ Gerald Koh and conservation educator John Chua surprise the teachers who inspired and guided them. Together, these emotional journeys celebrate friendship, gratitude and the lasting impact of those who quietly shape lives.

Twice a year, Asia’s coastlines enter a brief, rare window of extraordinary equinox “king tides” where the Sun, Moon and Earth align and the sea surges beyond its usual limits. In that short period, homes, sea walls, livelihoods and ecosystems are stress-tested and the shoreline becomes a moving border. Tides of Time is a three-part series narrated by BAFTA-nominated presenter and Sunday Times best-selling author Ben Fogle. Filmed in Bangladesh, China and South Korea, the team chases this celestial trigger along three epic shores where water doesn’t just rise but rewrites the communities’ destinies. From Sundarbans’ Hanging Homes Village, to China’s Qiantang “Silver Dragon” tidal bore, to Korea’s getbol mudflats, each film is a human rendezvous with the tide where humans must choose to adapt, resist or surrender.
From business to politics, health to technology, the latest news from Singapore and analysis of the impact.

What does it take for everyday hawker stalls to earn Michelin recognition, and can they keep their Bib Gourmand status? How has the accolade impacted the life of these humble hawkers? At Bahrakath Mutton Soup, sole chef Syed Abdul Rahaman grapples with passing down this award-winning taste to his sons as age creeps up on him. Over at Selamat Datang Warong Pak Sapari, second-generation owner Sumadi Sapari walks the tightrope between expanding the business and protecting the authenticity of his late father's recipe. For Koh Brother Pig Organ Soup, Thomas Koh left his career to carry on a family legacy. After failed franchising attempts, he's poured himself into making every bowl the best it can be. And at Chef Kang's Noodle House, brothers Benson and Winson Moo—disciples of Michelin-starred Chef Kang—have won, lost, and regained their Bib Gourmand. This year, the question looms: can they hold onto it?
The latest top stories of the hour.

Unfolding the pivotal moments of World War II, this documentary offers a powerful, minute-by-minute chronicle of the events that reshaped the modern world. From the surprise attack on Pearl Harbour that drew the United States into the global conflict, to the secretive and urgent race to develop the atomic bomb under the Manhattan Project, every stage is revealed with compelling detail. The story culminates in the harrowing aftermath of August 6, 1945, when Hiroshima was levelled by the first atomic weapon ever used in war. Through archive footage, expert insight. It’s a sobering reflection on the price of war and a world forever altered.
